                        << predicate.getQualifierDebug() << ", got: "
                        << (githubLatestRelease.assets |
                            ranges::view::transform(&aui::updater::github::LatestReleaseResponse::Asset::name));
                    return;
                }
                ALogger::info(LOG_TAG) << "To download: " << (mDownloadUrl = it->browser_download_url);

                getThread()->enqueue([this, self = shared_from_this(), version = githubLatestRelease.tag_name] {
                    if (AMessageBox::show(
                            nullptr, "New version found!", "Found version: {}\n\nWould you like to update?"_format(version),
                            AMessageBox::Icon::INFO, AMessageBox::Button::YES_NO) != AMessageBox::ResultButton::YES) {
                        return;
                    }

                    downloadUpdate();
                });

            } catch (const AException& e) {
                ALogger::err(LOG_TAG) << "Can't check for updates: " << e;
                getThread()->enqueue([] {
                    AMessageBox::show(
                        nullptr, "Oops!", "There is an error occurred while checking for updates. Please try again later.",
                        AMessageBox::Icon::CRITICAL);
                });
            }
        };
    }

    AFuture<void> downloadUpdateImpl(const APath& unpackedUpdateDir) override {
        return AUI_THREADPOOL {
          try {
              AUI_ASSERTX(!mDownloadUrl.empty(), "make a successful call to checkForUpdates first");
              downloadAndUnpack(mDownloadUrl, unpackedUpdateDir);
              reportReadyToApplyAndRestart(makeDefaultInstallationCmdline());
          } catch (const AException& e) {
              ALogger::err(LOG_TAG) << "Can't check for updates: " << e;
              getThread()->enqueue([] {
                AMessageBox::show(
                    nullptr, "Oops!", "There is an error occurred while downloading update. Please try again later.",
                    AMessageBox::Icon::CRITICAL);
              });
          }
        };
    }

private:
    AString mDownloadUrl;
};

downloadAndUnpack downloads the archive, reports progress to AUpdater::status and unpacks into unpackedUpdateDir. reportReadyToApplyAndRestart then switches the status to AUpdater::StatusWaitingForApplyAndRestart and remembers the command line to launch, so even if the user quits the app now, the update is applied on the next start.

Warning

Anonymous GitHub API requests are rate-limited per IP address. Do not check for updates more often than once per several hours, and never in a loop.

docs.title: Other sources
docs.text: Nothing in AUpdater is tied to GitHub. Fetch a JSON manifest from your server in checkForUpdatesImpl, remember the download URL in a member, and pass it to downloadAndUnpack in downloadUpdateImpl. Only a ZIP archive is understood by downloadAndUnpack; for other formats, unpack into unpackedUpdateDir yourself.

docs.title: Adding auto-update to an app
docs.text: This page walks through connecting AUpdater to an application. For the update process itself (what happens between checkForUpdates and the restart), see updater. To get releases that the updater can consume, see Publishing releases for AUpdater.

docs.title: Link the module
docs.text:
Add updater to the components of auib_import and link aui::updater. The module uses aui::curl, aui::json and aui::crypt internally, so list them as well.

auib_import(aui https://github.com/aui-framework/aui
        COMPONENTS core views curl json crypt updater
        VERSION ${AUI_VERSION})

aui_executable(${PROJECT_NAME})
aui_link(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE aui::core aui::views aui::curl aui::json aui::updater)

App Template ⚡ has this already set up, including GitHub Actions that publish releases.

docs.title: Subclass AUpdater
docs.text: AUpdater is a strategy: it handles the mechanics of unpacking and deploying, while you decide where updates come from by implementing checkForUpdatesImpl and downloadUpdateImpl. Both return an AFuture<void> and run on whatever thread you choose (typically a thread pool). A complete GitHub-based implementation is shown in Publishing releases for AUpdater.

docs.title: Call handleStartup first
docs.text:
handleStartup must be called as early as possible, before any window is shown. It processes the --aui-updater-* arguments passed by a previous instance of your app and, when an update is being deployed, terminates the process with std::exit(0).

class MyUpdater : public AUpdater {
protected:
    AFuture<void> checkForUpdatesImpl() override { return AUI_THREADPOOL { /* stub */ }; }
    AFuture<void> downloadUpdateImpl(const APath& unpackedUpdateDir) override { return AUI_THREADPOOL { /* stub */ }; }
};

AUI_ENTRY {
    auto updater = _new<MyUpdater>();
    updater->handleStartup(args);

    // your program routines (i.e., open a window)
    _new<MainWindow>(updater)->show();
    return 0;
}

Keep the updater instance alive for the lifetime of the application and pass it to the UI, see Update UI: progress, apply and restart.

docs.title: Check that the updater is available
docs.text:
AUpdater::isAvailable() returns false when the executable is not writable by the current user (i.e., installed to Program Files, or a system package), or the platform is unsupported. In that case AUpdater turns into a stub and sets its status to AUpdater::StatusNotAvailable. Hide update controls in that state instead of letting the user press buttons that do nothing:

if (!AUpdater::isAvailable()) {
    // do not show "Check for updates" button
}

docs.title: Version of your app
docs.text:
The versions are compared with aui::updater::Semver. For your own version, use the one from project(... VERSION x.y.z) in your root CMakeLists.txt: AUI passes it to every aui_executable and aui_module as the AUI_CMAKE_PROJECT_VERSION macro.

EXPECT_EQ(aui::updater::Semver::fromString("1.2.3"), (aui::updater::Semver{ 1, 2, 3 }));
EXPECT_EQ(aui::updater::Semver::fromString("1.2"), (aui::updater::Semver{ 1, 2, 0 }));
EXPECT_EQ(aui::updater::Semver::fromString("1"), (aui::updater::Semver{ 1, 0, 0 }));
//AUI_DOCS_CODE_END

// `v` prefix is acceptable:
//AUI_DOCS_CODE_BEGIN
EXPECT_EQ(aui::updater::Semver::fromString("v1.2.3"), (aui::updater::Semver{ 1, 2, 3 }));
EXPECT_EQ(aui::updater::Semver::fromString("v0.0.0"), (aui::updater::Semver{ 0, 0, 0 }));
//AUI_DOCS_CODE_END

// "Channel names" and other suffixes are ignored:
//AUI_DOCS_CODE_BEGIN
EXPECT_EQ(aui::updater::Semver::fromString("1.2.3-beta"), (aui::updater::Semver{ 1, 2, 3 }));

Only the three numeric components are compared; suffixes such as -beta are dropped, so 1.2.3-beta and 1.2.3 are the same version for the updater.

docs.title: Supported platforms
docs.text: Windows (portable ZIP, or an installer that installs into the user's directory) and Linux (portable ZIP) are supported. On macOS and mobile platforms the stores or your own distribution mechanism take care of updates. See updater for the full table.

docs.title: Unit-testing your UI
docs.text:
checkForUpdatesImpl and downloadUpdateImpl are pure virtual, so a GMock subclass is all that is needed to drive your UI without network access. Assign AUpdater::status directly to simulate a state, and change progress of StatusDownloading to simulate a download. The status view from Update UI: progress, apply and restart is tested this way in aui.updater/tests/UpdaterStatusTest.cpp; combine it with aui::uitests (see Writing tests) to click on the buttons.

class MyUpdater : public AUpdater {
public:
    MOCK_METHOD(AFuture<void>, checkForUpdatesImpl, (), (override));
    MOCK_METHOD(AFuture<void>, downloadUpdateImpl, (const APath& unpackedUpdateDir), (override));
};

docs.title: Testing version logic
docs.text: aui::updater::Semver and aui::updater::AppropriatePortablePackagePredicate are plain value types and are trivially testable; feed them tag names and file names captured from your real releases.

docs.title: Testing the deployment
docs.text:
The deployment replaces your application's files, so it cannot be tested in-process. The framework's own test (UpdaterTest.ApplyUpdate) launches a helper executable, aui.updater.test, with a --test=<dir> argument. A copy of the executable plus a marker file is placed in a temporary directory in advance, which imitates a downloaded update. The updater applies it, and the test checks the marker file appeared next to the original executable. To do the same in your app, override getUnpackedUpdateDir() and loadInstallCmdline() (protected virtuals of AUpdater) so the updater picks up a directory you prepared.

Note

The deployment test is compiled only for static AUI builds.

docs.title: Debugging a failed update
docs.text:
Deployment is performed by a separate process after your application exits, so errors do not show up in your log. The process id is logged by applyUpdateAndRestart, and the deployment log is the log file of that pid. See the "Debugging update deployment" section of AUpdater for an annotated example. A typical failure is "Text file busy" or "Access denied": the old process had not exited yet or an antivirus locks the file.

Common reasons why nothing happens:

  • AUpdater::isAvailable() is false: the executable is not writable, or the platform is unsupported.
  • The release has no archive matching the platform; getQualifierDebug() of the predicate prints what was expected.
  • The archive is not a ZIP, or does not contain the executable under the name returned by getModuleName().

docs.title: Update UI: progress, apply and restart
docs.text: AUpdater exposes everything the UI needs as one property, AUpdater::status. It holds one of the statuses AUpdater::StatusIdle, AUpdater::StatusCheckingForUpdates, AUpdater::StatusDownloading, AUpdater::StatusWaitingForApplyAndRestart or AUpdater::StatusNotAvailable (or your own type) in a std::any. It is updated in the UI thread only.

docs.title: Status-driven view
docs.text:
Project the status into views with readProjected: each time the status changes, the view is rebuilt. The downloading status carries a progress property that can be bound directly to AProgressBar; the bar then updates without rebuilding.

CustomLayout {} & mUpdater->status.readProjected([&updater = mUpdater](const std::any& status) -> _<AView> {
    if (std::any_cast<AUpdater::StatusIdle>(&status)) {
        return _new<AButton>("Check for updates").connect(&AView::clicked, AUI_SLOT(updater)::checkForUpdates);
    }
    if (std::any_cast<AUpdater::StatusCheckingForUpdates>(&status)) {
        return Label { "Checking for updates..." };
    }
    if (auto downloading = std::any_cast<AUpdater::StatusDownloading>(&status)) {
        return Vertical {
            Label { "Downloading..." },
            _new<AProgressBar>() & downloading->progress,
        };
    }
    if (std::any_cast<AUpdater::StatusWaitingForApplyAndRestart>(&status)) {
        return _new<AButton>("Apply update and restart")
            .connect(&AView::clicked, AUI_SLOT(updater)::applyUpdateAndRestart);
    }
    return nullptr;
}),

The buttons call checkForUpdates and applyUpdateAndRestart. applyUpdateAndRestart terminates the process, so save the user's data before calling it.

docs.title: Custom statuses
docs.text:
status is AProperty<std::any>, so you may assign your own struct, for example to display an error after a failed download. The updater does not interpret unknown types.

struct StatusFailed {
    AString reason;
};
updater->status = StatusFailed { "No internet connection" };

Reset the status to AUpdater::StatusIdle when the user dismisses the error, otherwise checkForUpdates stays unavailable (it requires StatusIdle).

docs.title: Choosing the workflow
docs.text: Whether to ask the user at every step or to download silently is up to you. See "Updater workflows" in updater. When downloading silently, call downloadUpdate() at the end of checkForUpdatesImpl, and show only a "Restart to update" button for StatusWaitingForApplyAndRestart. Avoid modal message boxes unless the user explicitly asked for the check.

docs.title: After the update
docs.text: On the first start of the updated application handleStartup removes the downloaded files. If the deployment failed, the old version is launched with --aui-updater-failed and the reason is available from AUpdater::getLastDeploymentError(), which you can show in the UI. See Testing and debugging AUpdater for debugging.

docs.title: aui::updater
docs.text: Deliver updates on non-centralized distribution methods

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
Experimental Feature

This API is experimental. Experimental APIs are likely to contain bugs, might be changed or removed in the future.

This module is purposed for delivering updates to your end users on distribution methods that do not support that by themselves (i.e., occasional Windows installers, portables for Windows and Linux, macOS app bundles downloaded from your website). Here's small breakdown:

Platform Distribution method Auto updating solution Windows (operating system) Installer/exe updater Windows (operating system) Microsoft Store (used rarely) Microsoft Store Linux (-based desktop OSes) Portables updater Linux (-based desktop OSes) Flatpak Flathub macOS (operating system) DMG (*.app) - macOS (operating system) Apple App Store Apple App Store Android (operating system) APK Google Play Store iOS (operating system) IPA Apple App Store What is portable?

Portable is a term used to describe a software distribution method that does not require the user to install the software on their computer.

Portable software is typically distributed as a single executable file (i.e., a single file with all dependencies packed into it), usually not requiring to "install" it to the system.

aui.updater module expects your program to be installed to user's directory (i.e., updating does not require admin privileges). If that's not your case, you'll need to update your installer configuration (Inno Setup) to install to user's directory (i.e., in AppData).

Note

Check out our App Template ⚡ for a GitHub-hosted app template with auto update implemented.

docs.title: Supported platforms
docs.text:
aui::updater supports the following platforms:

  • Windows - portables (AUI_PORTABLE_ZIP, AUI_PORTABLE_TGZ) only, installers to user's directory only (Inno Setup)
  • Linux - portables only

On a supported platform, aui::updater checks if the app executable is writable by the current user. If the executable is not writeable, or running on a non-supported platform, AUpdater stubs it's methods (i.e., they do nothing). You can check that the aui::updater functionality is engaged by calling AUpdater::isAvailable().

Updating process requires the initial application running instance to be stopped to replace its files with newer ones. Additionally, the updater process starts the newer version of the application after replacing the files (applying/deploying an update). To minimize downtime for end-users, the replacement should be seamless and quick and thus the deployment process just copies newer files (overwriting old ones), it does not involve network operations.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
AUpdater lives inside entrypoint of your application. It needs you to pass program arguments. It might decide to terminate process execution via std::exit. 

class MyUpdater : public AUpdater {
protected:
    AFuture<void> checkForUpdatesImpl() override { return AUI_THREADPOOL { /* stub */ }; }
    AFuture<void> downloadUpdateImpl(const APath& unpackedUpdateDir) override { return AUI_THREADPOOL { /* stub */ }; }
};

AUI_ENTRY {
    auto updater = _new<MyUpdater>();
    updater->handleStartup(args);

    // your program routines (i.e., open a window)
    _new<MainWindow>(updater)->show();
    return 0;
}
AUI_DOCS_CODE_BEGIN

You can pass updater instance to your window (as shown in the example) and display update information from AUpdater::status and perform the update when requested.

docs.title: Observing update progress
docs.text: See AUpdater::status

docs.title: Checking for updates
docs.text:
AUpdater expects AUpdater::checkForUpdates() to be called to check for updates. It can be called once per some period of time. It calls user-defined AUpdater::checkForUpdatesImpl() to perform an update checking.

The update steps are reported by changing AUpdater::status property.

sequenceDiagram
 autonumber
 participant a as Your App
 participant u as AUpdater

 a->>u: handleStartup(...)
 u-->>a: status = AUpdater::StatusIdle
 u-->>a: control flow

 Note over a,u: App Normal Lifecycle
 a->>u: checkForUpdates()
 u-->>a: status = AUpdater::StatusCheckingForUpdates
 u-->>a: control flow
 u->>u: checkForUpdatesImpl()
 u-->>a: status = AUpdater::StatusIdle

 Note over a,u: update published
 a->>u: checkForUpdates()
 u-->>a: status = AUpdater::StatusCheckingForUpdates
 u-->>a: control flow
 u->>u: checkForUpdatesImpl()
 Note over u: update was found
 u-->>a: status = AUpdater::StatusIdle

You might want to store update check results (i.e., download url) in your implementation of AUpdater::checkForUpdatesImpl so your AUpdater::downloadUpdateImpl() might reuse this information.

docs.title: Downloading the update
docs.text:
When an update is found, your app should call AUpdater::downloadUpdate() to download and unpack the update. It is up to you to decide when to download an update. If you wish, you can call AUpdater::downloadUpdate in AUpdater::checkForUpdatesImpl() to proceed to download process right after update was found (see Updater workflows for more information about update workflow decisions). It calls user-defined AUpdater::downloadUpdateImpl() which might choose to call default AUpdater::downloadAndUnpack(<YOUR DOWNLOAD URL>, unpackedUpdateDir).

sequenceDiagram
   autonumber
   participant a as Your App
   participant u as AUpdater

   a->>u: downloadUpdate()
   u-->>a: status = AUpdater::StatusDownloading
   u->>u: downloadUpdateImpl()
   u-->>a: status = AUpdater::StatusWaitingForApplyAndRestart

   Note over a,u: Your App Prompts User to Update

docs.title: Applying (deploying) the update
docs.text:
At this moment, AUpdater waits AUpdater::applyUpdateAndRestart() to be called. When AUpdater::applyUpdateAndRestart() is called (i.e., when user accepted update installation), AUpdater executes the newer copy of your app downloaded before with a special command line argument which is handled by AUpdater::handleStartup() in that executable. The initial app process is finished, closing your app window as well. From now, your app is in "downtime" state, so we need to apply the update and reopen app back again as quickly as possible. This action is required to perform update installation. The copy then replaces old application (where it actually installed) with itself (that is, the downloaded, newer copy). After operation is complete, it passes the control back to the updated application executable. At last, the newly updated application performs a cleanup after update.

sequenceDiagram
   autonumber
   participant a as Your App
   participant u as AUpdater
   u -->> a: applyUpdateAndRestart()
   create participant da as Your App Copy
   u -->> da: Execute with update arg
   u -->> u: exit(0)
   Note over a,u: Process Finished
   create participant du as AUpdater Copy
   da -->> du: handleStartup
   du -->> du: deployUpdate(...)
   du -->> a: Execute
   destroy du
   du -->> da: exit(0)
   destroy da
   da-->a:
   Note over a,u: Process Started
   a -->> u: handleStartup
   u -->> u: cleanup download dir
   a --x u: App Normal Lifecycle

After these operations complete, your app is running in its normal lifecycle.

docs.title: Typical Implementation
docs.text:
AUpdater is an abstract class; it needs some functions to be implemented by you.

In this example, let's implement auto update from GitHub release pages. 

static constexpr auto LOG_TAG = "MyUpdater";
class MyUpdater: public AUpdater {
public:
    ~MyUpdater() override = default;

protected:
    AFuture<void> checkForUpdatesImpl() override {
        return AUI_THREADPOOL {
            try {
                auto githubLatestRelease = aui::updater::github::latestRelease("aui-framework", "example_app");
                ALogger::info(LOG_TAG) << "Found latest release: " << githubLatestRelease.tag_name;
                auto ourVersion = aui::updater::Semver::fromString(AUI_PP_STRINGIZE(AUI_CMAKE_PROJECT_VERSION));
                auto theirVersion = aui::updater::Semver::fromString(githubLatestRelease.tag_name);

                if (theirVersion <= ourVersion) {
                    getThread()->enqueue([] {
                      AMessageBox::show(
                          nullptr, "No updates found", "You are running the latest version.", AMessageBox::Icon::INFO);
                    });
                    return;
                }
                aui::updater::AppropriatePortablePackagePredicate predicate {};
                auto it = ranges::find_if(
                    githubLatestRelease.assets, predicate, &aui::updater::github::LatestReleaseResponse::Asset::name);
                if (it == ranges::end(githubLatestRelease.assets)) {
                    ALogger::warn(LOG_TAG)
                        << "Newer version was found but a package appropriate for your platform is not available. "
                           "Expected: "
                        << predicate.getQualifierDebug() << ", got: "
                        << (githubLatestRelease.assets |
                            ranges::view::transform(&aui::updater::github::LatestReleaseResponse::Asset::name));
                    return;
                }
                ALogger::info(LOG_TAG) << "To download: " << (mDownloadUrl = it->browser_download_url);

                getThread()->enqueue([this, self = shared_from_this(), version = githubLatestRelease.tag_name] {
                    if (AMessageBox::show(
                            nullptr, "New version found!", "Found version: {}\n\nWould you like to update?"_format(version),
                            AMessageBox::Icon::INFO, AMessageBox::Button::YES_NO) != AMessageBox::ResultButton::YES) {
                        return;
                    }

                    downloadUpdate();
                });

            } catch (const AException& e) {
                ALogger::err(LOG_TAG) << "Can't check for updates: " << e;
                getThread()->enqueue([] {
                    AMessageBox::show(
                        nullptr, "Oops!", "There is an error occurred while checking for updates. Please try again later.",
                        AMessageBox::Icon::CRITICAL);
                });
            }
        };
    }

    AFuture<void> downloadUpdateImpl(const APath& unpackedUpdateDir) override {
        return AUI_THREADPOOL {
          try {
              AUI_ASSERTX(!mDownloadUrl.empty(), "make a successful call to checkForUpdates first");
              downloadAndUnpack(mDownloadUrl, unpackedUpdateDir);
              reportReadyToApplyAndRestart(makeDefaultInstallationCmdline());
          } catch (const AException& e) {
              ALogger::err(LOG_TAG) << "Can't check for updates: " << e;
              getThread()->enqueue([] {
                AMessageBox::show(
                    nullptr, "Oops!", "There is an error occurred while downloading update. Please try again later.",
                    AMessageBox::Icon::CRITICAL);
              });
          }
        };
    }

private:
    AString mDownloadUrl;
};
AUI_DOCS_CODE_BEGIN

docs.title: Updater workflows
docs.text:
When using AUpdater for your application, you need to consider several factors including usability, user experience, system resources, and particular needs of your project.

Either way, you might want to implement a way to disable auto update feature in your application.

docs.title: Prompt user on every step
docs.text:
This approach is implemented in AUI's App Template ⚡.

The updater checks for updater periodically or upon user request and informs the user that an update is available. The user then decides whether to proceed with update or not. If they agree the application will download and install the update.

This way can be considered as better approach because the user may feel they control the situation and the application never does things that user never asked to (trust concerns). On the other hand, such requirement of additional user interaction to can distract them from doing their work, so these interactions should not be annoying.

You should not use AMessageBox (unless user explicitly asked to check for update) as it literally interrupts the user's workflow, opting them to make a decision before they can continue their work. A great example of a bad auto update implementation is qBittorrent client on Windows: hence this application typically launches on OS startup, it checks for updates in background and pops the message box if update was found, even if user is focused on another application or away from keyboard.

docs.title: Silent download
docs.text:
This approach is implemented in AUI Telegram Client (AUIgram), as well as in official Qt-based Telegram Desktop client.

The updater silently downloads the update in the background while the user continues working within the application or even other tasks. The update then is applied automatically upon restart. Optionally, the application might show a button/message/notification bubble to restart and apply update.

Despite user trust concerns, this approach allows seamless experience - users don't need to be interrupted during their work. They even might not care about updates.

#include <AUI/UITest.h>
#include <AUI/Util/UIBuildingHelpers.h>
#include <AUI/View/AButton.h>
#include <ExampleWindow.h>
#include <AUI/View/ATextField.h>

/**
 * <p>
 *   A bug appeared in this example application related to AUI layout managers. This suite checks the following issues:
 * </p>
 * <ul>
 *   <li>height of the latest element sometimes (not always!) seems to be incorrect</li>
 *   <li>latest elements sometimes (again, not always!) seems to be not fit to the parent's border</li>
 * </ul>
 *
 * <p>Details: <a href="https://github.com/aui-framework/aui/issues/18">https://github.com/aui-framework/aui/issues/18</a></p>
 * <p>Photo:</p>
 * <img src="https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/19491414/144756936-173e5d65-9433-4c00-92d6-142ca217164d.png" />
 *
 */


class UILayoutManager: public testing::UITest {
public:
protected:
    void SetUp() override {
        UITest::SetUp();
        _new<ExampleWindow>()->show();
    }

    void TearDown() override {
        UITest::TearDown();
    }
};


/**
 * Checks height of all buttons - they should be the same (see "Show all views..." button above).
 */
TEST_F(UILayoutManager, Height) {
    // check height
    (By::text("Common button") | By::text("Show all views...")).check(sameHeight(), "height mismatch");
}


/**
 * Checks alignment (see "Alex2772, 2021, alex2772.ru" - it is not perfectly aligned)
 */
TEST_F(UILayoutManager, LastElementAlignment) {
    // copyright width can be also not minimal
    By::name("#copyright").check(widthIsMinimal(), "copyright width should be minimal");
}

/**
 * Checks alignment (looks like buttons and list views are not perfectly aligned)
 */
TEST_F(UILayoutManager, ButtonsAlignment) {
    // buttons column should be perfectly aligned
    By::name("Common button")
        .parent()
        .allChildren()
        .check(leftRightAligned(), "elements should be perfectly aligned");
}

void ExampleWindow::onDragDrop(const ADragNDrop::DropEvent& event) {
    ASurface::onDragDrop(event);

    for (const auto& [k, v] : event.data.data()) {
        ALogger::info("Drop") << "[" << k << "] = " << AString::fromUtf8(v);
    }

    auto surface = createOverlappingSurface({ 0, 0 }, { 100, 100 }, false);
    _<AViewContainer> popup = Vertical {
        Label { "Drop event" } AUI_OVERRIDE_STYLE {
              FontSize { 18_pt },
              ATextAlign::CENTER,
            },
        [&]() -> _<AView> {
            if (auto u = event.data.urls()) {
                auto url = u->first();
                if (auto icon = ADesktop::iconOfFile(url.path())) {
                    return Centered { _new<ADrawableView>(icon) AUI_OVERRIDE_STYLE { FixedSize { 64_dp } } };
                }
            }
            return nullptr;
        }(),
        AText::fromString("Caught drop event. See the logger output for contents.") AUI_OVERRIDE_STYLE { ATextAlign::CENTER, MinSize { 100_dp, 40_dp } },
        Centered { Button { Label { "OK" }, [surface] { surface->close(); } } },
    };
    ALayoutInflater::inflate(surface, popup);
    popup->pack();

    surface->setOverlappingSurfaceSize(popup->size());
    surface->setOverlappingSurfacePosition((size() - *popup->size()) / 2);
}

bool ExampleWindow::onDragEnter(const ADragNDrop::EnterEvent& event) { return true; }

#include "DemoGraphView.h"
#include <AUI/ASS/ASS.h>

constexpr auto POINT_COUNT = 100.f;

DemoGraphView::DemoGraphView()
{
    setFixedSize({ 5_dp * POINT_COUNT, 100_dp }); // set fixed size


    mPoints.reserve(POINT_COUNT);
    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < POINT_COUNT; ++i) {
        // map a sinusoid to view
        mPoints << glm::vec2{ 5_dp * float(i), 100_dp * ((glm::sin(i / 10.f) + 1.f) / 2.f) };
    }
}

void DemoGraphView::render(ARenderContext ctx) {
    AView::render(ctx);

    ctx.render.lines(ASolidBrush{0xff0000_rgb }, mPoints, ABorderStyle::Dashed{}, 4_dp);

}

AString DemoListModel::listItemAt(const AListModelIndex& index) {
    return "List item #{}"_format(index.getRow() + 1);

void DemoListModel::addItem() {
    mListSize += 1;
    emit dataInserted(range({mListSize - 1}));
}

void DemoListModel::removeItem() {
    if (mListSize > 0) {
        mListSize -= 1;
        emit dataRemoved(range({mListSize}));
    }
}

docs.title: Windows (operating system)
docs.text: Windows is a family of operating systems developed by Microsoft. It was first released in 1985 and has since become the most popular desktop operating system worldwide, with a market share of about 70%. The latest version for consumer PCs and tablets is Windows 11, while certain older versions are still supported and maintained by Microsoft.

docs.title: Windows XP support
docs.text:
• If ucrtbase.dll is missing, download and place it next to folder where it is missing.
  • Compatibility with modern C++ (MSVC v143+ C++20 standard or newer) is provided by YY_Thunks project (span, concepts).
  • aui.boot relies over v141_xp toolset and cl.exe compiler with UCRT runtime by VC-LTL5, that are specified by winxp-x86.cmake cmake toolchain file.
  • google/benchmark is removed, as v141_xp toolset was unable to build that dependency, because #include <versionhelpers.h> is missing.
  • Windows XP support lower bound is SP2, as SP1 is not supported.
  • In order to bring your own dependencies you would need to use /MT /MTd MSVC runtime and acquire UCRT runtime by VC-LTL5.
  • If you are searching for v141_xp toolset download link take a look here https://aka.ms/vs/16/release/vs_buildtools.exe.

docs.title: Key considerations
docs.text:
• You'll need to make an installer and potentially a portable package with auto updating to distribute your application despite Windows offers an "official" software repository
  • Windows is the only system that is not Unix-like, despite it provides POSIX-compliant APIs
  • You might need to sign your executables, otherwise Windows would probably treat your application as a virus and make launching your executables a lot harder

docs.title: AUI implementation specifics
docs.text: • Single instance (Application lifetime & instancing): AApplication::requestSingleInstanceLock creates a session-local mutex Local\aui.<key>.<sessionId> and listens on the named pipe \\.\pipe\aui.<key>.<sessionId>. The secondary instance calls AllowSetForegroundWindow(ASFW_ANY) before forwarding its activation, so the primary is allowed to call SetForegroundWindow (see AWindow::activate).

docs.title: Writing tests
docs.text:
AUI uses GTest as the tests framework and provides a simple way to use it in your application.

It also includes GMock library.

GoogleTest is Google's C++ testing and mocking framework. This user's guide has the following contents:

  • GoogleTest Primer - Teaches you how to write simple tests using GoogleTest. Read this first if you are new to GoogleTest.
  • GoogleTest Advanced - Read this when you've finished the Primer and want to utilize GoogleTest to its full potential.
  • GoogleTest Samples - Describes some GoogleTest samples.
  • GoogleTest FAQ - Have a question? Want some tips? Check here first.
  • Mocking for Dummies - Teaches you how to create mock objects and use them in tests.
  • Mocking Cookbook - Includes tips and approaches to common mocking use cases.
  • Mocking Cheat Sheet - A handy reference for matchers, actions, invariants, and more.
  • Mocking FAQ - Contains answers to some mocking-specific questions.

docs.title: In AUI
docs.text: In order to enable tests for your project, call aui_enable_tests(<target-name>) in the end of your CMakeLists.txt and create tests/ dir along with src/ and CMakeLists.txt. Place your test suites inside the tests/ directory.

docs.title: Usage Example
docs.text:
Suppose we want to test the sum function of the following program:

main.cpp
#include <AUI/Platform/Entry.h>
#include <AUI/Logging/ALogger.h>
#include "main.h"

static constexpr auto LOG_TAG = "MyApp";

int sum(int a, int b) {
  return a + b;
}

AUI_ENTRY {
    ALogger::info(LOG_TAG) << "2 + 2 = " << sum(2, 2);
    return 0;
}

Possible output:

[14:57:02][UI Thread][MyApp][INFO]: 2 + 2 = 4

docs.title: Project structure
docs.text:
To write a test, enable tests for your projects first. Add aui_enable_tests(<target-name>) to the end of your CMakeLists.txt:

CMakeLists.txt
# Standard routine
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
project(project_template)

# Use AUI.Boot
#
# Download aui.boot.cmake (one-time):
#   curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aui-framework/aui/refs/heads/master/aui.boot.cmake -o aui.boot.cmake
#
# Or use CLI mode:
#   cmake -P aui.boot.cmake update
#
include(aui.boot.cmake)

# link AUI
auib_import(
    AUI https://github.com/aui-framework/aui 
    COMPONENTS core)


# Create the executable. This function automatically links all sources from the src/ folder, creates CMake target and
# places the resulting executable to bin/ folder.
aui_executable(project_template)

# Link required libs
target_link_libraries(project_template PRIVATE aui::core)

aui_enable_tests(project_template) # <----------------------------------------------

and create the tests/ dir along with CMakeLists.txt and src/. Inside tests/, create MyTest.cpp:

tree
CMakeLists.txt
src
├── main.cpp
└── main.h
tests
└── MyTest.cpp

Note the main.h file. Since we would like to access the sum function of main.cpp, we should put sum declaration to the main.h file:

main.h
#pragma once

int sum(int a, int b);

Put the basic test case to MyTest.cpp:

MyTest.cpp
#include <gtest/gtest.h>
#include "main.h"

TEST(MyTest, Sum) {
  ASSERT_EQ(sum(2, 2), 4);
}

Build Tests and run bin/Tests. Possible output:

Console
[==========] Running 1 test from 1 test suite.
[----------] Global test environment set-up.
[----------] 1 test from MyTest
[ RUN      ] MyTest.Sum
[       OK ] MyTest.Sum (0 ms)
[----------] 1 test from MyTest (0 ms total)

[----------] Global test environment tear-down
[==========] 1 test from 1 test suite ran. (0 ms total)
[  PASSED  ] 1 test.

AUI does the following fundamental things for you:

  1. Collect all tests from your tests/ dir
  2. Provide an entry point for the Tests program (testing::InitGoogleTest)
  3. Mirror all linked libraries and compile options to the Tests program
  4. If you are testing a shared library, the shared library is linked to the Tests program
  5. If you are testing an executable, the executable's sources are automatically compiled with the Tests program and the include scope of the executable is copied to the Tests program (this is why we have easily accessed the main.h header)

docs.title: Writing UI Tests
docs.text:
Since AUI is a UI framework it is also capable of UI tests.

In addition to the previous example, we'd create some window:

UITest.cpp
#include <AUI/UITest.h>
#include <AUI/Util/UIBuildingHelpers.h>
#include <AUI/View/AButton.h>
#include <AUI/Platform/AWindow.h>
#include <AUI/View/ATextField.h>
#include <AUI/View/AScrollArea.h>
#include <gmock/gmock.h>

class TestWindow: public AWindow {
public:
    TestWindow() {
        setContents(Centered {
            _new<AButton>("Hello!")
        });
    }
};

class UIScrollTest: public testing::UITest {
public:
protected:

    class TestWindow: public AWindow {
    public:
        TestWindow(): AWindow("Test window", 200_dp, 100_dp) {
            setContents(Vertical {
                    AScrollArea::Builder().withContents(_new<MockedViewContainer>()).withExpanding().build()
            });
        }
    };
    _<TestWindow> mTestWindow;


    void SetUp() override {
        UITest::SetUp();

        // prepare the window
        mTestWindow = _new<TestWindow>();
        mTestWindow->show();
    }
};

docs.title: Parsing XML
docs.text:
This page shows how to read XML with aui::xml. The parser is event-driven: AXml::read pulls bytes from an input stream and reports attributes, text and nested elements to visitor objects you provide. Nothing is stored for you, so you decide what to keep.

Interface Receives IXmlDocumentVisitor top-level elements and the <?xml ... ?> header IXmlEntityVisitor attributes, text and nested elements of a single element IXmlHeaderVisitor attributes of the <?xml ... ?> header

docs.title: Reading attributes
docs.text:
Given a file like this:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<settings>
    <window width="800" height="600" title="Demo"/>
</settings>

create one visitor per element you are interested in. visitEntity returns the visitor for the element it was called for; the parser then feeds that element's attributes and children into it.

#include <AUI/Xml/AXml.h>
#include <AUI/IO/AFileInputStream.h>

// ignores an element and everything inside of it; see "Ignoring elements"
struct IgnoreVisitor: IXmlEntityVisitor {
    _<IXmlEntityVisitor> visitEntity(AString entityName) override {
        return _new<IgnoreVisitor>();
    }
};

struct WindowVisitor: IXmlEntityVisitor {
    int width = 0;
    int height = 0;
    AString title;

    void visitAttribute(const AString& name, AString value) override {
        if (name == "width") {
            width = value.toInt().valueOr(0);
        } else if (name == "height") {
            height = value.toInt().valueOr(0);
        } else if (name == "title") {
            title = std::move(value);
        }
    }
};

struct SettingsVisitor: IXmlEntityVisitor {
    _<WindowVisitor> window;

    _<IXmlEntityVisitor> visitEntity(AString entityName) override {
        if (entityName == "window") {
            window = _new<WindowVisitor>();
            return window;
        }
        return _new<IgnoreVisitor>();
    }
};

struct DocumentVisitor: IXmlDocumentVisitor {
    _<SettingsVisitor> settings;

    _<IXmlEntityVisitor> visitEntity(AString entityName) override {
        settings = _new<SettingsVisitor>();
        return settings;
    }
};

auto document = _new<DocumentVisitor>();
AXml::read(_new<AFileInputStream>("settings.xml"), document);
// document->settings->window->width == 800

Visitors are plain objects: keep the results in their fields and read them after AXml::read returns. Attributes are reported in the order they appear. An attribute without a value (<input disabled>) is reported with an empty string.

Attribute values come as AString; use toInt() / toDouble() for numbers, which return an AOptional.

docs.title: Reading from a string
docs.text:
AXml::read takes an IInputStream, so a string needs to be wrapped in an AStringStream:

#include <AUI/IO/AStringStream.h>

AXml::read(_new<AStringStream>(AString(R"(<item id="1"/>)")), document);

docs.title: Text and nested elements
docs.text:
visitTextEntity is called with the text between tags, and visitEntity for each nested element. The calls follow document order, so a visitor can accumulate a list of children and text pieces:

struct ListVisitor: IXmlEntityVisitor {
    AVector<AString> items;

    _<IXmlEntityVisitor> visitEntity(AString entityName) override {
        items << std::move(entityName);
        return _new<IgnoreVisitor>();
    }
};

Text that consists of whitespace only (indentation, line breaks) is reported too, and so can be empty strings between adjacent elements; filter them out with trim() if you only care about meaningful text.

docs.title: Ignoring elements
docs.text:
To ignore an element along with all of its attributes, text and children, return nullptr from visitEntity. The parser still reads the element through to its closing tag, so the rest of the document is parsed as usual.

struct Visitor: IXmlEntityVisitor {
    _<IXmlEntityVisitor> visitEntity(AString entityName) override {
        if (entityName == "debug") {
            return nullptr;   // <debug>...</debug> is skipped
        }
        return _new<Visitor>();
    }
};

docs.title: The XML header
docs.text:
IXmlDocumentVisitor additionally has visitHeader, called for <?xml ... ?>. The default implementation returns nullptr, which ignores the header (unlike elements, this is safe). Return an IXmlHeaderVisitor to get its attributes:

struct HeaderVisitor: IXmlHeaderVisitor {
    void visitAttribute(const AString& name, const AString& value) override {
        ALogger::info("Xml") << name << " = " << value;   // version = 1.0, encoding = UTF-8
    }
};

struct DocumentVisitor: IXmlDocumentVisitor {
    _<IXmlHeaderVisitor> visitHeader() override {
        return _new<HeaderVisitor>();
    }
    // ...
};

docs.title: Handling errors
docs.text:
A malformed document makes AXml::read throw AXmlParseError, which derives from std::runtime_error:

try {
    AXml::read(_new<AStringStream>(AString("<item id=1/>")), document);
} catch (const AXmlParseError& e) {
    ALogger::err("Xml") << "Bad xml: " << e.what();
}

The parser is lenient: it throws only when an attribute value is not quoted or a closing tag is malformed. A truncated document ends silently at the end of the input without an error, so do not rely on the exception to validate documents.

The error message ends with the position of the offending character in the form row:column.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
aui::xml is a minimal parser (it is what AText uses for its HTML-like markup), not a full XML implementation. Be aware of the following:

  • Element names may consist of letters and digits only: my-tag, my_tag and ns:tag are not recognized. Attribute names may additionally contain :.
  • XML entities (&, <, 
) are not decoded; you receive them as is. Instead, backslash escapes (\n, \t, \\, \uXXXX) are processed in text and attribute values, as in other AUI tokenizers, which a regular XML document does not expect. A literal backslash in the data is therefore best avoided.
  • Comments (<!-- -->), <![CDATA[ ]]> and <!DOCTYPE> are not supported.
  • Namespaces, schemas and validation are not supported.
  • There is no XML writer. To produce XML, build the string yourself, escaping &, <, > and quotes.

If you need more than this, use a dedicated XML library and import it with AUI.Boot (see aui.boot).

docs.title: aui::xml
docs.text: XML parser library.

docs.title: Detailed Description
docs.text:
aui::xml is a small event-driven (SAX-like) XML reader. It does not build a document tree; instead, AXml::read walks the input once and reports everything it meets to your visitors:

  • IXmlDocumentVisitor receives the top-level elements and, optionally, the <?xml ... ?> header;
  • IXmlEntityVisitor receives attributes, text and nested elements of one element;
  • IXmlHeaderVisitor receives the attributes of the <?xml ... ?> header.
#include <AUI/Xml/AXml.h>
#include <AUI/IO/AStringStream.h>

struct Item: IXmlEntityVisitor {
    void visitAttribute(const AString& name, AString value) override {
        ALogger::info("Xml") << name << " = " << value;
    }
};

struct Document: IXmlDocumentVisitor {
    _<IXmlEntityVisitor> visitEntity(AString entityName) override {
        return _new<Item>();
    }
};

AXml::read(_new<AStringStream>(AString("<item id=\"1\" title=\"Hello\"/>")), _new<Document>());

To link aui::xml to your project, add the xml component to auib_import and link aui::xml:

auib_import(aui https://github.com/aui-framework/aui COMPONENTS core xml VERSION ${AUI_VERSION})
aui_link(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE aui::xml)

See Parsing XML for a walkthrough and the limitations of the parser. There is no XML writer in aui::xml.
